title: Memory controls
description: The operator's own controls over what memory keeps and what it surfaces — deliberately a SEPARATE contract from recall. Recall is a read: `search` is described as never changing or removing what is stored, and that description has to stay true, so the operations that deliberately write belong under their own boundary rather than smuggled in beside the ones that do not. Three things a caller can ask for, each on the operator's explicit say-so and never inferred: pin something so it is kept and carried into later sessions; withhold a note or a whole conversation so recall stops surfacing it; and put a withheld thing back. Nothing here deletes: withholding leaves every record in the ledger exactly as it was, and restoring is always available. Permanent erasure IS part of this contract — as a command-line verb that no tool serves, so it is not reachable from any of the served operations — it requires merging a single-purpose erasure pull request, which no caller of these operations can do. A pin records the route it arrived by rather than any claim about who authored it: a model calling `pin` is transcribing what the operator asked for, and its context may also hold text it recalled or read, so no reader may present a pin as verified wording.

operations.name: pin
operations.description: Save a standing instruction the operator wants kept — a preference, a way of working, a decision with no better home. Deliberate and small by design: pins are the one thing nothing ages out and nothing summarises away, and they are carried into the start of later sessions, so this is invoked when the operator asks for something to be remembered, never inferred from the shape of a conversation. The text is scrubbed of secret-shaped content before it is stored. Over-long text is refused rather than shortened, because a silently halved instruction is worse than one that was not saved.

text.description: The standing instruction to keep, in the operator's own terms.

session_id.description: The session it was asked for in, so the conversation around the request stays reachable. Omit when there is none.

id.description: The pin's stable identifier, as `withhold` would name it.

text.description: What was stored, after scrubbing — which may differ from what was passed in.

pinned_via.description: The route it arrived by. A route, never a claim about authorship.

operations.name: list-pins
operations.description: Read back every pin the operator currently has saved, newest first. Declared because the session-start briefing tells them they can ask to see all of them — a promise nothing could keep while the only way to enumerate pins was a Python call. It also carries the count, which the briefing's bounded sample cannot: a caller that has seen five pins has no way to know whether that is all of them.

total.description: How many there are, so a bounded view can say what it left out.

operations.name: withhold
operations.description: Stop recall surfacing one note, or one whole conversation. Reversible and non-destructive: every record stays in the ledger byte for byte, and `restore` brings it back. It reaches every way memory is read — ranked search, meaning-based search, the session reader, and the summary a new session is oriented from — so a withheld conversation is not merely unsearchable but unquoted. Exactly one of the two targets is named; a request naming both, or neither, is refused rather than guessed at.

record_id.description: A single record, as carried on a search result or listed among the pins.

session_id.description: A whole conversation, as carried on a search result.

withheld.description: What is now out of recall, in plain words the caller can relay.

operations.name: list-withheld
operations.description: Read back what the operator currently has out of recall, named so it can be restored. Declared because every surface promises a withhold is reversible and `restore` needs the exact identifier the withhold used — a promise that held only while the session that performed the withhold still had that identifier in its context. Returns identifiers and when, never the wording: reading withheld text back is the thing the operator asked not to happen.

operations.name: restore
operations.description: Put back something the operator withheld, by the same target the withhold named. Restoring something that was never withheld is harmless rather than an error, so "put it back" is safe to say twice. It cannot recover anything erased — erasure is a different act under a different gate, and nothing here reaches it.

record_id.description: The single record to bring back.

session_id.description: The whole conversation to bring back.

restored.description: What is surfaced again, in plain words the caller can relay.

operations.name: erase
operations.description: Permanently erase what the operator names — the one act in this contract with no undo, and the only one that is NOT reachable from a tool. It is a command-line verb that refuses unless it is attached to a controlling terminal, prints the target's own words, and waits for a typed confirmation. That refusal is the barrier, not a courtesy: an automated caller has no terminal, so no model path reaches the confirmation. It is declared here because it is one of the operator's controls and a reader of this contract must know it exists and where it is; it is declared as NOT SERVED because an implementation that exposed it as a callable tool would defeat the thing that makes it safe. Nothing is erased when it runs: it writes a content-free proposal and opens a single-purpose pull request, and only the operator's merge of that pull request carries the erasure out, in a later session. The target must already be withheld from recall — the reversible act always precedes the irreversible one, though that is a guard against a mistake rather than a gate against an attacker, because nothing downstream re-checks it. NOT SERVED AS A TOOL: it is reached only from the command line only (tools/memory/erase.py), by a person at a terminal.

target.description: A record id, or a session id to erase a whole conversation.

status.description: proposed | declined | written | retry — never 'erased', because this operation never erases.

operations.name: rescrub
operations.description: Run every stored record back through the secret masking. Capture masks secret-shaped text before anything is written, but only for what was captured after that masking existed; everything stored before it went in raw. This is the operator-asked verb that fixes that, and it is a verb rather than something that runs on upgrade because it rewrites the operator's own conversation and should ask first. It refuses unless a backup destination is configured, takes a copy before touching anything, holds the single-writer lock across the whole rewrite so no turn captured meanwhile is lost, and verifies the result three ways before replacing the original. It refuses outright if any line of the store cannot be parsed, rather than dropping it. Declared NOT SERVED for the same reason as erase: it rewrites stored data, and the consent for that belongs with a person, not a tool call. NOT SERVED AS A TOOL: it is reached only from the command line only (tools/memory/rescrub.py plan | run).
